## Overview

Compare a TF-IDF classifier with an LLM on the same sentiment classification task using 20 sample reviews.

## Task 1: Select 20 Test Reviews

Choose 20 reviews (10 positive, 10 negative) from your test set. These should include some easy cases and some tricky ones (sarcasm, negation, mixed sentiment).

## Task 2: Classify with Your TF-IDF Model

```{python, warning=FALSE}
# Use your pipeline from P12.1
import pandas as pd, joblib

pipe = joblib.load("tfidf_pipe.joblib")
test = pd.read_csv("imdb_test_split.csv")
short = test[test["text"].str.len() < 700]

pat = r"\b(?:but|however|although|though|despite|except|yet|not)\b|n't"

def pick(label):
    pool = short[short.label == label]
    tricky = pool[pool.text.str.contains(pat, case=False, regex=True)].sample(5, random_state=1)
    regular = pool.drop(tricky.index).sample(5, random_state=1)
    return pd.concat([tricky.assign(kind="tricky"), regular.assign(kind="regular")])

sample = pd.concat([pick(0), pick(1)]).sample(frac=1, random_state=1).reset_index(drop=True)
sample.insert(0, "review_id", range(1, 21))
sample.to_csv("rp12_2_sample20.csv", index=False)

# Print these and paste them into the LLM
for _, r in sample.iterrows():
    print(f"{r.review_id}. {r.text}\n")
    
sample["tfidf_pred"] = pipe.predict(sample["text"])
```

## Task 3: Classify with an LLM

Use Claude, ChatGPT, or another LLM (via web interface or API) to classify the same 20 reviews. Document the prompt you used.

**Your prompt:** *Classify each movie review below as Positive or Negative. Reply with only a numbered list (1-20), one word per line: Positive or Negative.*

```{python}
# llm outputs
raw = """1. Negative
2. Positive
3. Negative
4. Positive
5. Negative
6. Positive
7. Negative
8. Positive
9. Negative
10. Negative
11. Positive
12. Negative
13. Positive
14. Positive
15. Negative
16. Positive
17. Negative
18. Positive
19. Positive
20. Negative"""

llm_preds = [1 if "Positive" in line else 0 for line in raw.splitlines()]
assert len(llm_preds) == 20
```

## Task 4: Compare Results

```{python}
sample["llm_pred"] = llm_preds
sample["tfidf_ok"] = sample.tfidf_pred == sample.label
sample["llm_ok"] = sample.llm_pred == sample.label
sample["both_correct"] = sample.tfidf_ok & sample.llm_ok

name = {0: "neg", 1: "pos"}
table = sample[["review_id", "label", "tfidf_pred", "llm_pred", "both_correct"]].copy()
for c in ["label", "tfidf_pred", "llm_pred"]:
    table[c] = table[c].map(name)
table["both_correct"] = table["both_correct"].map({True: "Y", False: "N"})
table.columns = ["Review #", "True Label", "TF-IDF Prediction", "LLM Prediction", "Both Correct?"]
table
```

**Summary:**
- TF-IDF accuracy on these 20: 16/20
- LLM accuracy on these 20: 20/20

## Task 5: Error Analysis

```{python}
diff = sample[sample.tfidf_ok != sample.llm_ok]
for _, r in diff.iterrows():
    who = "TF-IDF failed, LLM right" if r.llm_ok else "LLM failed, TF-IDF right"
    print(f"#{r.review_id} ({who}), true={name[r.label]}\n{r.text}\n")
```

For cases where one method failed and the other succeeded, explain WHY:

**TF-IDF failed, LLM succeeded:**
> *TF-IDF missed four reviews (#3, #6, #11, #19). In each, the words that carry the sentiment don’t match the surface vocabulary the model learned, which is what a bag-of-words model sees.*

**LLM failed, TF-IDF succeeded (if any):**
> *none*

## Task 6: Reflection (150 words)

When would you choose TF-IDF over an LLM? When would you choose the LLM? Consider: cost, speed, accuracy, interpretability, and data privacy.

> *I would choose TF-IDF when I need to classify large volumes of text cheaply, quickly, and privately. It trains in seconds, runs locally with no per-query cost, and is interpretable: I can inspect coefficients to see exactly why a review was labeled negative, as I did in P12.1. Because the data never leaves my machine, it is also the safer choice for sensitive text. However, my comparison showed its weakness. It missed 4 of 20 reviews because it counts words without understanding context, so it was fooled by negative topics, ironic praise, and hedged criticism. The LLM got 20 out of 20 by reading tone and overall verdict, so I would choose it for small, high-stakes, or nuanced tasks where accuracy matters most. Its downsides are cost, slower speed, privacy risk from sending data to a third party, and less transparent reasoning. With only 20 reviews, these results are suggestive, not conclusive.*
